items.followUp: Differentiate between linear motion and rotatory motion.

rubric.why: Circular motion is motion along a circular path around an external point.
rubric.how: Award for describing motion along a circular path around a point outside the body.

rubric.why: Rotatory motion is rotation about an axis passing through the body.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the body rotates about an axis passing through itself.

modelAnswer: In circular motion, a body moves along a circular path around a point outside the body.
In rotatory motion, a body rotates about an axis passing through itself.

items.followUp: What is meant by an ideal rigid body?

rubric.why: A rigid body retains its shape and size when a force acts on it.
rubric.description: States that a rigid body does not change shape or size.
rubric.how: Award for saying that its shape and size do not change under the action of a force.

rubric.why: The distance between any two points of an ideal rigid body remains constant.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the distance between any two points or particles remains constant.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body whose shape and size do not change when a force acts on it.
The distance between any two points of a rigid body remains constant.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a solar cell and a solar panel?

rubric.why: A solar cell converts sunlight directly into electrical energy.
rubric.description: States the function of a solar cell.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that a solar cell converts sunlight into electricity.

rubric.why: A solar panel is made up of many solar cells.
rubric.description: Distinguishes a panel from a single solar cell.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a solar panel consists of a group or number of solar cells.

modelAnswer: A solar cell is a device that converts sunlight directly into electrical energy.
A solar panel consists of many solar cells connected together.
